formData.team:
3rd Man is built and led solo by me, Paul Kaberere I'm the project lead and sole developer across the whole stack. That covers the Rust/Axum backend (auth, KYC, agreements, negotiation, collateral, escrow, disputes, points, ledger), the React/Vite/TypeScript frontend (wallet integration, agreement wizard, milestone delivery, arbiter console, governance panel), and the on-chain Aiken (Plutus V3) validator, including the Pallas-based Rust transaction builder wired to Cardano Preprod testnet.

We've already budgeted for a third-party smart contract security audit ahead of mainnet deployment this is a precondition for the M1 milestone, since the validator will be holding real user funds. I've reached out to Invariant0, the Cardano audit team with a scoping email covering the validator's architecture, its current Preprod-tested status, and our 3-month mainnet timeline. I'm now waiting on their reply about availability and cost before we can lock in a schedule. I'll also bring on a legal/compliance advisor for Kenyan financial regulation on the escrow/custody model, on the same near-term timeline, once I've identified specific candidates.

Links: Paul Kaberere — [github.com/paloxmah0](http://github.com/paloxmah0)
formData.giveBack: We pledge 2% of net transaction fee revenue back to the Catalyst treasury, activating once monthly fee revenue exceeds 500 ADA ensuring the give-back reflects genuine, sustained usage, not pilot-phase test activity. Completion of the Adoption phase and project close using the declared measurement structure: a one-epoch entry ramp from your M1 delivery, then six floored 5-day epochs - with extra epochs earned by delivering early - under the Standard's per-epoch floors and daily cap. The whole project completes within the program's four-month frame.

Your declared adoption targets, restated from your answers. They drive the M2 payout and the Transaction Integrity checks, and are final at submission:

- Oracles: 200 transactions expected, 300 ADA in counted fees
- On-chain identity (CIP-0170): 150 transactions expected, 100 ADA in counted fees

**Acceptance criteria**

1. The measurement window ran as declared at M1 delivery: the one-epoch entry ramp plus your floored epochs, including any extra epochs earned by early delivery.
2. Per-epoch floors observed, with at most the Standard's one free miss.
3. Counted totals respect the daily cap: a single day may exceed the Standard's share of your measurement-period total, but the excess does not count toward it.
4. At least the Standard's minimum of distinct external wallets transacted with your integration during the window.
5. All measured activity derives from the declared identifiers and complies with the [Transaction Integrity Standard](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard#transaction-integrity-standard).

**Evidence of milestone completion**

1. Adoption summary statement: your actuals against each declared target.
2. Per-epoch table: epoch number, date range, transactions and counted fees, daily cap applied (y/n), floor met (y/n), notes.
3. Raw explorer and dashboard links for the declared identifiers.
4. Short methodology note: how counts and fees were derived from the declared identifiers.
5. A completion video (1-3 mins) is shared via YouTube showcasing the project outputs.
6. Any additional cross-checks.
formData.usagePlan: Our first users are Nairobi freelancers and secondhand-goods sellers doing real P2P deals reached first through the Cardano NBO Blockchain Centre's existing Web3 community, then Nairobi's WhatsApp/Facebook Marketplace trading groups, where escrow demand is already proven by competitors like Shikilia and TrustPay. This is a deliberately global product proven locally first: the same non-custodial mechanic applies anywhere P2P trust is a problem, and Kenya is where we validate it before extending to other mobile-money markets. Each user registers on-chain identity (CIP-0170) once per wallet this sets the 150 target, matched to our realistic first-cohort size across these channels. Oracle transactions come from delivery/condition confirmation: not every escrow needs one, since simple pay-on-confirmation deals settle peer-to-peer, but staged/freelance work and delivery-dependent sales the higher-friction deals oracles exist to solve do, at roughly 1.3 oracle calls per active user across the adoption window, giving 200 total. Both targets sit modestly above floor rather than being padded, because they're built from named, already-warm channels, not a generic marketing funnel.
formData.goToMarket: We launch in Kenya first, then extend to other mobile-money markets once the model is proven. Our first channel is the Cardano NBO Blockchain Centre's existing Nairobi Web3 community a warm, already-assembled group, not a cold audience. Beyond that, we're targeting Nairobi's existing secondhand/freelance WhatsApp and Facebook Marketplace trading groups directly the same channels TrustPay and Shikilia already use to reach this exact user base, which tells us the channel converts. Once usage is proven in Kenya, the same non-custodial model ports directly to other mobile-money economies (e.g. Nigeria, Ghana, the Philippines) with the same trading-group and community-first playbook. We do not yet have signed letters of intent, and we are stating that plainly rather than overclaiming

formData.competitors: This space has real answers already, locally and globally: Kenya Escrow, TrustPay KE, eConfirm, and Shikilia offer M-Pesa escrow for Jiji/WhatsApp/freelance deals, and globally [Escrow.com](http://Escrow.com) and PayPal's buyer protection serve the same need in card/bank-based markets. They prove demand exists — but every one is custodial: your money sits in a company's account, and you're trusting that business not to misuse, freeze, or lose it. That's the exact "just another middleman" problem we're removing. 3rd Man is non-custodial: funds sit in a Cardano smart contract tied to the user's own wallet, so no team, including ours, can access or override them the same advantage anywhere in the world. Users switch for the same reason people move from trusting a company to trusting code.

formData.architecture:
The system splits into on-chain and off-chain layers: the off-chain layer (Rust/Axum backend) handles everything that doesn't need trustlessness — wallet-native auth, negotiation, notifications, dispute routing — while custody of funds lives in the deployed Aiken Plutus V3 validator, not the backend. Wallet-native auth uses CIP-8 COSE_Sign1 parsing and Ed25519 verification, so users authenticate by signing with their Cardano wallet, with identity as did:cardano:

 derived directly from the wallet — the right fit for on-chain identity (CIP-0170) since the DID is already anchored to a cryptographic signature, not a database record. Transactions are constructed with Pallas (Rust) — real Babbage-era CBOR built and submitted server-side via Koios, with no browser-side or Lucid dependency — keeping the trust-critical transaction logic inside the same audited codebase as the rest of the backend. The validator itself handles Deposit, ClaimUnit, SubmitProof, ReviewProof, RaiseDispute, ArbiterResolve, and Refund natively, so dispute resolution — exactly where oracle condition-verification is needed — is enforced on-chain via Ed25519-verified oracle-signed data, not bolted on after the fact. Config carries the deployed script hash and address as first-class values the backend points at, consistent with non-custodial design and Cardano's eUTXO model.
formData.targetMarket: The P2P trust gap is global anywhere a buyer and seller don't fully know each other, someone has to go first. It's sharpest in mobile-money-driven, informal-commerce economies: Kenya's informal sector alone is roughly 18.1M people (\~84% of employment), and the same pattern  heavy mobile money use, thin formal escrow, large informal/gig commerce repeats across Sub-Saharan Africa, South/Southeast Asia, and Latin America. We launch in Kenya first: Nairobi freelancers and secondhand-goods sellers trading over WhatsApp, where at least four M-Pesa escrow products already operate itself demand evidence. Kenya is our proof market; the model extends to any mobile-money-first market.
formData.businessModel: Revenue is a small % fee taken on release of escrowed funds the same model TrustPay, Shikilia, and [Escrow.com](http://Escrow.com) already validate as accepted globally for this exact service. The difference is where that fee lives: settlement happens on-chain, so network fee volume from 3rd Man transactions is directly, verifiably measurable on Cardano, not something we can inflate in a report, regardless of which market it comes from. Usage should persist post-pilot because the underlying need doesn't expire in any market every new P2P deal recreates the same trust problem and switching to non-custodial escrow is a one-way improvement: once someone stops worrying about a company holding their money, they don't go back. The pilot in Kenya proves the fee-per-transaction economics at real volume before we extend the same model to other mobile-money markets

formData.m1Deliverables: By end of the 3-month window: (1) Aiken escrow validator completed, audited for basic logic errors, and deployed to Cardano mainnet, holding funds in a script address tied to user wallets, not a company account. (2) CIP-0170 on-chain identity integrated into the existing auth flow users register their DID on-chain via wallet signature (CIP-8 verification already built). (3) Oracle integration live for delivery/condition confirmation on staged and delivery-dependent deals. (4) Existing Rust/Axum backend (agreements, collateral, escrow, dispute modules) fully wired to the deployed validator, replacing placeholder config with real script hash/address. (5) At least one real user completes a full escrow deal end-to-end on mainnet create, pay, lock, confirm, release  repeated across independent runs. (6) Public repo, release notes, and technical walkthrough video published.
formData.problemSolution: We're building 3rd Man, an automated escrow system that solves a problem most people doing business with a stranger have faced, anywhere in the world: nobody wants to pay first, and nobody wants to deliver first. If you're buying something secondhand, hiring a freelancer, or paying for work in stages, you're stuck in a standoff. The usual fix is finding someone both sides trust to hold the money until the deal is done a "third man." It works, but only if you know someone trustworthy who's willing to do it, and even then they could be slow, unavailable, or dishonest. 3rd Man replaces that person with a smart contract on Cardano holding payment until both sides confirm the deal is done, except it can't be bribed and can't run off with the money. You create a deal, share a link over any messaging app, and pay through whichever rail is native to your market mobile money like M-Pesa, or card/bank rails elsewhere. Funds lock automatically once payment lands, and release once the condition is met, with a real dispute process if something goes wrong. The trust gap this solves exists globally, but is sharpest in mobile-money, informal-commerce markets. We launch first in Kenya, where the gap is easiest to prove, then extend to other mobile-money markets worldwide.
formData.trlIntegrationEvidence:
Oracles (TRL 3): the oracle endpoint (POST /disputes/:id/oracle) exists and feeds arbiter decisions as non-fatal evidence; the Aiken validator's ArbiterResolve action already supports oracle-signed data via Ed25519 verification. Remaining: wiring a real decentralized oracle (Charli3 or Orcfax) for delivery confirmation, and moving oracle data on-chain as a required release input, not just off-chain arbiter evidence. On-chain identity CIP-0170 (TRL 4): did:cardano:

 generation from wallet signatures works, with KYC tiering and per-field privacy preferences already enforced. Remaining: full CIP-0170 DID document compliance (resolution endpoint, verification methods, service endpoints) and on-chain attestation anchoring via CIP-10 metadata transactions.

campaign.briefFull:
## **Overview**

Catalyst Pilot pays teams in ADA for real, verified usage on Cardano. Grants run from **50,000 to 200,000 ADA**, paid **40% to build** your integration, up to **40% on the adoption it earns**, and **20% for holding that usage** afterwards. Top performers also share a **separate bonus pool**. Adoption is measured in real network fees from real users, not self-reported metrics, so the money follows genuine usage, not vanity numbers.

It is a fast, focused round with one job: get a new Cardano integration live on mainnet and earning real fees. The grant is an enabler to kickstart that, not to cover end-to-end costs. Marketing-only proposals cannot be funded, the first milestone is a working integration, but marketing matters enormously afterwards, because it drives the usage that earns the adoption payment.

Teams that show real mainnet adoption are well positioned for what comes next, including potential support from the Cardano Foundation's [Venture Hub](https://cardanofoundation.org/venture-hub) and other specialised tracks in the wider ecosystem such as the [Draper Dragon](https://www.draperdragon.com/)-managed [Orion Fund](https://orion.draperdragon.com/) and associated instruments (e.g. [Cometa Labs](https://www.cometalabs.com/), [Draper U](https://draperuniversity.com/)).

---

## **Who can apply**

This pilot is for **teams with a mature product** who want to add a Cardano area of interest to it.

* **You have a real, working product**, validated on a public testnet or already live, on Cardano or another chain (roughly **TRL 5 or above**; [the TRL Guide](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/integration-guides) explains the concept of Technology Readiness Levels).
* **The integration is new work.** The grant funds you to build it, from the ground up to mainnet, and drive real usage. It must be live with real transactions by pilot end.
* It must be **genuine, incremental development**, not retroactive funding or research alone. Open source is preferred, not required.

**Submission limits.** One proposal per applicant, whether an individual, organisation, or consortium, and you cannot split into multiple entities to get around it. No individual may be named on more than one proposal in any delivery role, so a shared contributor cannot be spread across teams. This counts your project team, not the providers you integrate: many teams can build on the same oracle or stablecoin. Submit more than one and only the first counts; every participant's role must be disclosed. Read [Fund Rules](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/fund-rules) to learn more.

**Good standing.** Newcomers from other ecosystems are unaffected by this. But if you already deliver Catalyst-funded work, you cannot apply if any active project is more than 90 days behind, or over 12 months old and still incomplete (unless the Fund Operator has accepted a valid reason), or if you run more than three active Catalyst projects. Applicants must be 18 or over and complete identity verification (KYC/KYB). Read [Fund Rules](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/fund-rules) to learn more.

---

## **Areas of Interest**

Your proposal must leverage **at least one**:

* **Oracles**: real-time price feeds (for example, Pyth).
* **Stablecoins**: building with or accepting verified stablecoin policies (for example, USDM, USDCx), especially paths that move stablecoins from centralised exchanges onto Cardano.
* **Programmable tokens (CIP-0113)**: tokens with embedded logic, for example real-world-asset tokenisation with compliance rules.
* **On-chain identity (CIP-0170)**: wallet and stake-key-based identity.

[The Integration Guides](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/integration-guides) cover each one, with docs and starting points. Every project must clear its category's **program floor**, a minimum level of counted network fees; floors and target guidance are in [the Proof of Adoption & Standard](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard).

**Dune Analytics** is a mandatory tracking add-on, not an integration in itself: every funded project tags its transactions with a standardised label, so its activity feeds a central "Catalyst Impact" dashboard and the [public leaderboard](https://cardano.org/apps/leaderboard/).

---

## **Funding and milestones**

Your grant (50,000 to 200,000 ADA) is paid in three parts, and top performers earn a bonus on top:

| Part | Share | Paid when |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Build | 40% | At onboarding |
| Adoption | up to 40% | After your measurement window, on the usage you earned |
| Kicker | 20% | About two months later, if your usage holds |
| Bonus | up to 50% of your grant | Top adoption performers only, from a separate pool |

* **Total pool: 2,500,000 ADA**, 2,000,000 in base grants, a 400,000 bonus pool for top performers, and 100,000 for ecosystem-supporting activities (separate from the bonus).
* **Cohort: about 10 to 15 teams, subject to proposal quality**.
* Your requested amount sets your **adoption floor** and your **external-wallet minimum**, both shown to you when you declare your target.

The three steps:

1. **Onboarding (KYC/KYB)** unlocks the 40% build payment. Complete it, with an approved Statement of Milestones, within **two weeks** of award, or the grant may be withdrawn, so come ready to move.
2. **Milestone 1, technical delivery (within 3 months).** Your integration is live on Cardano mainnet, proven by a real on-chain transaction. No payment attaches; this is your Demo Day, where you lock your adoption target and declare what counts ([Standard §4](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard)). Mainnet by this point is required whatever readiness you started from.
3. **Milestone 2, adoption.** Your measurement period runs from Milestone 1 to the program's end at **month 4**, the same for everyone, so delivering early gives you a longer window against the same target. Reach your target and the full 40% adoption payment pays; land between the floor and your target and it pays proportionally; finish below the floor and it doesn't pay. The full mechanics, floors, pace, and timing, are in the Standard ([§7, §8, §10](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard)).

---

## **What your proposal must include**

1. **Product and problem**: what you're building and why it matters.
2. **Market and business case**: the landscape, and why now.
3. **Team and traction**: why you're positioned to deliver, with verifiable profiles and roles.
4. **Build plan**: a concrete route to Milestone 1 within three months.
5. **Integration selection**: which area(s), and how you'll use them.
6. **Fee target and usage model**: your self-declared target per area (above the floor, final at submission), your expected transaction count, and where the usage comes from, named channels, existing users, and partner commitments, with rough volumes.
7. **Pace awareness**: that you understand usage has to hold a steady rhythm through the window ([Standard §7](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard)), and your plan for the first two weeks after going live.
8. **Recommended**: a three-minute pitch video.

---

## **How proposals are selected**

Every proposal passes an eligibility check during curation, then a scoring pass on two fronts: a **technical review** (is the integration sound and buildable to mainnet?) and a **business review** (is there real demand, a credible route to users, and usage that lasts?). Funding decisions are made by a **decision panel** of institutional and community members, whose assessments are merged into a single outcome; the top-ranked eligible proposals that fit the budget and cohort are then selected. Targets are scored both ways: too timid loses points, and too aggressive without evidence loses points too. The funding pool is a ceiling, not a quota: if too few proposals meet the bar, the program funds fewer teams than the target cohort and may reallocate the remainder to future rounds. Applying does not guarantee funding. Learn more about [Curation](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/curation) and [Decision](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/decision) stages.

---

## **Playing it straight**

This pilot pays for authentic utility, not vanity metrics. **The golden rule: if a simple script across a handful of your own wallets could reproduce your volume, it doesn't count.** Anyone can confidentially flag suspected misconduct; unproven flags are never published, and confirmed reports earn a reward. A confirmed case removes the activity and recalculates payments; a confirmed case of paying for or faking transactions forfeits every unpaid amount, with consequences that attach to the named individuals. Full detail is in [the Proof of Adoption & Standard](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard).

---

## **Anything else?**

Your proposal, progress reports, and proofs of achievement are published publicly. Before applying, read the [**Fund Rules**](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/fund-rules) and [**Terms and Conditions**](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/fine-print/terms-and-conditions), which govern funding, payment, and termination and prevail in any conflict. For this round, the payment and milestone structure set out in this Brief and the [**Proof of Adoption & Standard**](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard) is what applies.

Go deeper:

* [**Integration Guides**](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/integration-guides): what to build in each area, with docs and the TRL guide.
* [**Proof of Adoption & Standard**](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard): the floors, targets, and every counting rule.
* [**Pre-Submission Checklist**](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/pre-submission-checklist): run it before you submit.

All applicants must disclose their project team's roles and scope of services across all submitted proposals. Failure to disclose this information may lead to disqualification from the current fund round.

support.content: Choose at least one. Each selected integration is measured against its own adoption bar, and your milestone clears on the average across them. The [Integration Guides](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/integration-guides) explain what each involves.

support.title: Product Technology readiness
support.content: This grant is for teams with a mature product. Your existing product must be validated on a public testnet or live, in the Cardano ecosystem or another, TRL 5 or above. Rate it and link the evidence. Read [the full TRL guide here](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/technology-readiness-levels).

support.title: Integration Technology readiness
support.content: Most teams are at or near zero here when they apply, that's expected; this grant funds building the integration. Tell us where it stands now and what exists (design, prototype, testnet work), so we understand how much ground the grant covers. This does not gate your application; your build plan (following questions) is what's assessed.

support.title: Architecture
support.content: This is about design and suitability. Provide some technical context that shows your technical architecture is ready and suited for your solution.

support.title: What the funding changes
support.content: Be specific about what this money changes: what gets built or accelerated that otherwise wouldn't, and roughly where the funds go. Grants don't fund already-completed work.

support.title: Declaring targets
support.content: You declare two numbers per integration: 1. how many transactions you expect in the adoption phase of your project, and 2. your fee target - the total network fees, in ADA, those transactions will generate. Your program floor and wallet minimum are shown [here](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard#transaction-integrity-standard); your target must exceed the floor. Targets are frozen at submission, published, and scored for ambition.
support.subtitle: Per selected integration: expected transaction count + fee target (ADA)

support.title: Genuine usage
support.content: Describe the real usage: who transacts, why, at what cadence, and how you'll reach the projected transaction/fee targets you declared in your previous answers. Proposals with artificially low or otherwise unrealistic targets will be filtered out during the selection process.

support.title: Transaction Integrity Standard
support.content: Read the [Transaction Integrity Standard](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard#transaction-integrity-standard) before ticking - it defines what counts, what doesn't, and the one rule that matters most. Ticking is a formal attestation. Part of M1 output where this will be formalized - in form of wallets/scripts/policy footprints, etc.

options.checkboxLabel: Our plan complies with the [Transaction Integrity Standard](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard#transaction-integrity-standard)

support.title: M1 outputs
support.content: Non-negotiable: by the end of this window you must have a product deployed on mainnet, producing transactions, that real users can use. List concrete, measurable deliverables. This becomes your formal milestone statement verbatim at onboarding - scope can be added later, never reduced.

support.title: M1 acceptance evidence
support.content: This section is auto-populated. Evidence must be on-chain verifiable. At delivery you'll declare your on-chain identifiers, message tag, and team wallets - and your public daily chart starts counting from that moment. Demo Day doubles as the end of your development phase and the start of your Adoption phase - an important checkpoint to demonstrate what you have built before the final stage. Learn more about this in [Proof of Adoption & Standard](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard).

support.title: Adoption target at M2
support.content: This section is auto-populated - this combines your declared targets with the fixed measurement period: six 5-day floored epochs, beginning after a one-epoch entry ramp from your M1 delivery; with per-epoch floors, a daily cap, and extra epochs earned by delivering early. Confirm it reads as you intend. You have up to three months to deliver the technical part of your project. If you finish sooner, you benefit from a longer adoption window during M2. The whole project must complete within a four month time frame.

support.title: Give-back pledge
support.content: Entirely voluntary. If your product wins, you can pledge to return part of the grant, or share revenue with the Cardano treasury, once thresholds you set are hit. Pledges are viewed favorably and published if you're funded.

support.title: Before you submit
support.content:
Run this before you submit. At this stage you have a product, a plan, and a declared target, you haven't built the integration or generated any usage yet, and that's expected. So this checklist doesn't ask what you've delivered. It asks the two things review will judge from your proposal: **are you eligible, and is your proposal strong enough to fund?**

Answer honestly. If you can't tick a box, that's the thing to fix before you submit.

**How this connects to review.** The items in Section A are exactly what curators flag against at the compliance stage; if you can tick them, you clear the gate. Section B is what makes an eligible proposal a strong one, which the Decision panel scores.

support.title: B. Will it stand out?
support.content: Eligibility gets you considered; these get you funded. The Decision panel scores a **technical review** and a **business review**, and your team runs through both.

support.title: Other funding
support.content: Co-funding is not disqualifying, but the same deliverables cannot be funded twice, and work already delivered cannot be funded in this program. Tell us where the lines are.

support.title: Current commitments
support.content: Answering "No" is itself a declaration that no such commitments exist. Good standing on everything you list is required; standing on Catalyst-side projects is verified against program records.

support.title: Terms
support.content: Read, familiarize yourself with, and accept these terms.

options.checkboxLabel: **One proposal.** This is our only proposal, and no individual on our team, in any role (lead, member, subcontractor, or service provider), is named on another. We're not splitting across entities to get around the limit.

**Good standing.** Either we've never had Catalyst funding, or our record is clean: nothing more than 90 days behind or over 12 months incomplete (unless the Fund Operator has accepted a valid reason), and no more than three active Catalyst projects. Either way, we've disclosed all our active funding commitments, and any funding, past or present, for the same or substantially similar work.

**Named, verifiable team.** Every team member and key contributor is named, with their role on the project stated; their profiles (LinkedIn, GitHub, portfolio, references) are real and checkable; and we've disclosed each member's involvement across every proposal this round.
**Eligible area.** We use at least one: Oracles, Stablecoins, CIP-0113, or CIP-0170.

**Mature product.** Our existing product is at **TRL 5 or above**, validated on a public testnet or live, and the evidence is linkable. We're not relying on the integration's maturity; that's the new work the grant funds.
**Fits the timeline.** Our plan reaches mainnet within a credible 3-month build window and completes within the 4-month pilot.

**Genuine new work.** The budget is for future activities only, not retroactive funding, and we're not planning a prohibited use: paying or incentivising users to transact (ada giveaways, airdrops, transact-to-earn), speculation, or re-granting.
**Clear budget.** Our budget has a real breakdown tied to deliverables.

**Real target.** Our declared target can be defended as ambitious but realistic (the form enforces the floor; ambition is scored both ways), and we understand it is **final at submission** and published next to what we deliver.

**Real users.** We've named **where usage will come from**, channels, existing users, partners, with rough volumes, including our plan for the first two weeks after going live. Our usage model is built on real external users; we understand fees from our own or sponsored wallets won't count.

**Identified dependencies.** Any third parties we depend on are named with evidence the relationship exists. (The standard providers we integrate, an oracle or a stablecoin, are not partners and need no proof.)
**Standard read and attested.** We've read the **Proof of Adoption & Standard** and can honestly attest our plan complies.

**Public proposal.** We understand our proposal and all its contents are published publicly, along with our progress reports and results, and we've obtained any consent needed before including third-party or confidential information.
**Team.** We've evidenced why this team can deliver this specific work: relevant track record, prior shipped products, named roles, not just titles or a list of names.
**Technical.** Our architecture is sound and buildable to mainnet within three months, and we've shown it, not just described it.

**Business.** We've shown real demand with evidence, named our competitors and why users switch or activate, and explained durable usage. Our business case shows why usage **persists after the grant**, not just during the measurement period.

I confirm that I have read, understood and shall adhere to the [Terms & Conditions](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/fine-print/terms-and-conditions), [Fund Rules](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/fund-rules), [Proof of Adoption & Standard](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/funding-basics/proof-of-adoption-and-standard), and [Privacy Policy](https://docs.projectcatalyst.io/open-funding/fine-print/privacy-policy).
